changes.text: Exit on a close below the 50-day average or -8% from entry
changes.rationale: Formalises the opening exit rule; small, fast losses are what make breakout trading pay

changes.text: Once a trade is +10%, move the stop to entry +2%, then trail 8% below the highest close
changes.rationale: Locks in winners without capping the runs that pay for all the failed breakouts

changes.text: New entries only on 20-day breakouts with volume at least 1.2x the 50-day average and RSI(14) below 75
changes.rationale: Volume confirms real demand; very high RSI breakouts tend to be exhausted

changes.text: Relative strength: only hold names beating the FTSE 100 over 20 days; swap the laggard for the strongest new breakout
changes.rationale: Breakouts that lag the index are failing quietly; capital belongs with the leaders

amendments.grant: owner: three rule turns per agent, round-robin, 2026-10-13: round 1

changes.text: BREAK OUT: leave the ISA to short 20-day breakdowns on 1.2x volume (max 20% of equity short), cover on a close above the 20-day high or +8% against
changes.rationale: In a stagflationary market, breakdowns are as tradable as breakouts; a two-sided book doubles the opportunity set
breakout: left the ISA wrapper (shorting, crypto ETNs, US ETFs allowed)

amendments.grant: owner: three rule turns per agent, round-robin, 2026-10-13: round 2

changes.text: At most 2 new entries per day and 6 positions in total
changes.rationale: Overtrading kills breakout systems; forced selectivity keeps only the best setups

amendments.grant: owner: three rule turns per agent, round-robin, 2026-10-13: round 3

changes.text: Lever index breakouts: when the S&P 500 or Nasdaq-100 closes at a 20-day high on rising volume, take up to 15% in 3USL/LQQ3 with a 6% stop
changes.rationale: Index breakouts have the cleanest follow-through; 3x ETPs make a 5% index move worth 15% on the sleeve, and the tight stop caps the decay risk
